River Road Efficiencies

Under Agreement BCFB 1013, Walter Sprague Orchards used a $200,000 SWEEP award — matched by $47,859 of its own funds — to modernize the four-well irrigation system serving 167 acres of almonds and walnuts on River Road, Chico: new rotator sprinklers, soil-moisture telemetry, rebuilt pump discharges with flow meters, variable-frequency drives, and a 65 kW solar array to power it all. This dashboard reads the contract, the budget, and twelve geotagged field photographs together as one story: what was promised, what it cost, and what now stands in the orchard.

The agreement

From signature to field verification

Butte County Farm Bureau awarded the project under its CDFA SWEEP block grant. The scope of work names every component photographed below; payment terms hold back 10% ($20,000) until the completed project is verified. The site itself has seen drought in seven of the last ten years — including 25 weeks of 2021 under the U.S. Drought Monitor's most extreme Exceptional Drought designation.

The site walk

Twelve photographs in eighteen minutes, each stamped by GPS Map Camera. The coordinates trace a route across four distinct pump and equipment stations — consistent with the four-well layout the contract describes — from the west wellheads on River Road to the solar array and telemetry masts in the eastern blocks.

Solar / Renewable Energy
$110,000.00grant · + $47,255.00 rebate match

A 65 kW array now carries the pumping load

Contract scope

"WSO will install an Alternative Energy Solutions, Inc. solar system to power the four irrigation well pumps. This conversion … will result in a substantive reduction in emissions." Capacity: 65 kW (64.8 kW per budget worksheet).

Budget lines

AES agricultural ground-mount system, materials$110,000.00
Match: renewable rebates & incentives (cash)$47,255.00
Grant subtotal$110,000.00
Pump & Energy Improvements
$76,351.71grant

Four wells, rebuilt to measure and modulate

Contract scope

VFDs on Pump #3 (30 HP Layne & Bowler) and Pump #4 (Peerless); new filters, discharge assemblies, and flow meters on Pumps #1, #2, and #4 — Pump #3 already metered. Wells: #1 40 HP, #2 50 HP Johnston, #3 30 HP, #4 60 HP, together irrigating all 167 acres.

Irrigation Water Management
$7,737.65grant

Soil moisture data, delivered by sunlight and 4G

Contract scope

Two EnviroPro soil-moisture sensors measuring moisture, temperature, and salinity through the root zone, each on a solar-powered RTU relaying to phone or computer over 4G — the data backbone for irrigation scheduling on actual crop need.

Budget lines

EnviroPro soil moisture sensors × 2$3,284.00
Solar set, RTU 9V 5W × 2$500.00
RTU A760 4G LTE × 2$3,180.00
Sales tax$261.15
Contractor labor$512.50
Grant subtotal$7,737.65

"Updated rotor sprinklers to replace the old, leaky impact sprinklers in Block B" — 640 Nelson R2000 rotator kits, the smallest budget line but the most visible change in the tree rows.
